messages:
incident-bot: ALERT — Elevated 5xx rate detected on api-gateway-us-west-2
incident-bot: alert_id=igw-502-spike-1750056789 window=1m error_rate=17% threshold=5% triggered_by=rate-watchdog
sara-ops: paging oncall, joining. spike looks like 502/504s at edge->gateway, started ~09:10 PT
mike-sre: i'm on. dashboards show ingress burst to /v1/generate and /v1/stream; tcp retries and some upstream resets
jade-frontend: frontends report surge in pending connections, streaming clients timing out :grimacing:
leo-platform: any deploys right before spike? I see a small proxy tweak rolled at 09:05 by deploy-bot
sara-ops: @deploy-bot what changed? saw conn_timeout adjusted in proxy config at 09:05
deploy-bot: deploy_id=deploy-pt-772; change=proxy-tcp-timeout; status=success; smoke=pass
sara-ops: rolling rollback to rule out deploy impact — /deploy rollback proxy-config us-west-2 --author=deploy-bot
incident-bot: rollback queued, rolling across gateway nodes. ETA ~45s
emma-support: support queue getting error reports, ~10 customers flagged in last 12m. opening p0 threads for top impacted tenants
mike-sre: sampling logs: upstream model hosts intermittently returning 502 and some 504. connection pool exhaustion hints in nginx errs
jade-frontend: timeline: ingress latency increased first, then backend 502s spiked
mike-sre: quick health check:
```bash
curl -s -D - https://api.us-west-2.redwood-inference.com/v1/health
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
Content-Type: application/json
{"error":"upstream response: 502"}
```
leo-platform: rollback didn't drop errors immediately, looks like different root cause
sara-ops: pulling top source IPs to see if it's a fanout
mike-sre: logs snippet:
2026-02-17T09:10:12Z api-gw us-west-2 src=54.33.21.99 path=/v1/generate status=502 rt=1432ms
2026-02-17T09:10:13Z api-gw us-west-2 src=203.0.113.5 path=/v1/generate status=502 rt=1200ms
2026-02-17T09:10:14Z api-gw us-west-2 src=54.33.21.99 path=/v1/generate status=502 rt=1600ms

sara-ops: 54.33.21.99 maps to internal-eval-batch-runner. paging infra oncall
oncall-rotations: infra oncall here. I see a throughput test kicked at 09:08 that fans out to many tenants — probably the cause
mike-sre: makes sense — a high-fanout job starving connection pools and model hosts, leading to upstream resets and 502s
sara-ops: mitigation plan: 1) apply IP throttle at edge for offending source 2) pause the batch job 3) scale gateway pods 4) temporary nginx keepalive/conn bump 5) inform customers
jade-frontend: applying edge ACL throttle for 54.33.21.99 -> limit 25rps
```cfg
edge-acl apply --src 54.33.21.99 --limit 25
```
incident-bot: edge-acl change submitted change_id=acl-1750056801
mike-sre: scaling gateway: kubectl -n prod scale deploy/api-gateway --replicas=9
```bash
kubectl -n prod scale deploy/api-gateway --replicas=9
```
leo-platform: scaling reduced queue depth; error rate dropped from 17% -> ~8% in 2m
sara-ops: infra, can you pause that batch?
infra-oncall: paused the job at 09:14 PT, confirmed kill and backlog drained
emma-support: affected customers list: acme-inc, quickpay, scribbleai, blueapp, makerlabs — opening messages and posting status page update
jade-frontend: after ACL and pause, 5xx dropped to ~2.5%, still seeing some streaming timeouts
mike-sre: nginx errors show "upstream prematurely closed connection (110: Connection timed out)" and worker fd exhaustion in some nodes
sara-ops: propose temporary nginx tweaks: proxy_connect_timeout 60s -> 90s; keepalive 32 -> 48; worker_rlimit_nofile bump
sara-ops: config patch:
```nginx
proxy_connect_timeout 60s;
proxy_read_timeout 120s;
keepalive_timeout 85s;
upstream model_pool {
  keepalive 48;
}
```
incident-bot: config patch submitted via config-service; canary rollout to 2 nodes
leo-platform: canary looks good, no regressions; rolling to rest of cluster
jade-frontend: monitoring: 5xx now ~0.9% over last 5m, streaming errors mostly cleared
emma-support: customer notification sent: subject: "Degraded API availability in US-WEST-2 — Mitigation in progress" body: "We are mitigating elevated 502/504 errors. A misconfigured internal throughput test caused load spikes; we've throttled the source and scaled capacity. We'll follow up with RCA."
mike-sre: post-incident followups: - add hard limit for internal batch runners targeting prod - implement circuit-breaker at gateway for high-fanout endpoints - add deploy canary tests for conn-limit changes - postmortem
sara-ops: severity: Sev2 (partial outage affecting subset of tenants). postmortem owner: @mike-sre
oncall-rotations: infra to add guardrail preventing internal-runner fanout to production endpoints without quota. I'll follow up by EOD
leo-platform: short-term rule: block internal-runner pools from public prod APIs until guardrail is in place
sara-ops: timeline: 09:10 alert -> 09:14 job paused -> 09:16 ACL & scale -> 09:19 config roll -> 09:24 majority mitigated
emma-support: support updates sent to customers at 09:20 PT; follow-up to be shared after postmortem
mike-sre: collecting artifacts now: dashboards, nginx logs, kube events, deploy history. archiving to s3://redwood-incidents/1750056789
jade-frontend: note: proxy rollback earlier didn't help; root cause was the eval fanout. good catch to check logs quickly
sara-ops: next steps: 1) postmortem writeup with detailed timeline + RCA 2) automated fanout detector and throttle 3) permanent guardrail for internal-runner 4) canary load test for proxy changes
mike-sre: i'll draft the postmortem and share by EOD; tagging rca, mitigations, followups
emma-support: will prepare customer-facing summary after postmortem draft
sara-ops: leaving handoff: monitor 5xx <1.5% for 30m before closure. watch for any internal-job retries that might bypass ACLs
oncall-rotations: acknowledged — infra will push permanent guardrails and follow up in the postmortem
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — mitigations applied, error rate returned near baseline. monitoring for regressions for 1h
sara-ops: closing live triage, will reopen thread if anything spikes again. :thumbsup:
